title: Go-live approval notes, escalation & log mapping
content:
Purpose:
This is a working notebook for the go-live approval lane for the upcoming production launch (model-serving rollout). It is intentionally informal — captures signoff checklist, escalation points, audit log-field mapping for SIEM export, and the exception/fast-approval flow we want to trial for the next two weeks.

Summary (tl;dr):
- Primary ask: ensure RBAC v2 enactment, audit log coverage, and SIEM export mappings are validated with sample payloads.
- Secondary: wire evidence automation so that the release checklist bundles (logs + attestations) are produced automatically and attach to the release record.
- Tertiary: run the emergency exception approval path (two-on-call + SecEng lead) in a dry-run.

1) Key signoff checklist (manual + automated checkpoints)
- RBAC v2 policies applied to new serving endpoints: verify policy IDs and policy inheritance (lines-of-business) (owner: eng-privsec).
- Test users from 3 roles (platform-admin, infra-observer, customer-support) confirmed can/cannot perform the expected operations. Document screenshots or CLI traces.
- Audit log completeness: confirm every token to model allocation, model-pull, config-change, and rollout action emits an audit event.
- SIEM export: sample payloads (see examples below) sent to SIEM dev pipeline; confirm field mappings and retention tag.
- Evidence bundle packaging: evidence automation should produce a zip named RELEASE_EVIDENCE_<release-id>_YYYYMMDD containing logs, RBAC policy snapshots, and signoff.csv.
- Fallback plan: canary rollback tested end-to-end (owner: release-engineering).
- Exception approvals: test fast-path exception for one non-prod feature with retro review (owner: product-security).

2) Audit log schema (working mapping)
NOTE: this is a shorthand mapping for the SIEM team. Submit changes to the canonical Confluence doc above.
- timestamp: iso8601 UTC
- event_id: UUIDv4 correlated to request_id
- request_id: client-visible request id (if present)
- actor_id: internal user/service id (uin)
- actor_type: human | service | api-key
- actor_role: canonical role name (from RBAC v2 policy)
- resource: resource path (e.g. /models/redwood-v2/serving/instance-23)
- action: create|read|update|delete|serve|cache-invalidate|config-rollout
- outcome: success|failure|denied|timeout
- outcome_code: numeric internal classification (see Confluence mapping table)
- ip: originating ip or NAT gateway id
- region: data-center region tag
- kv_cache_hint: optional, key name for KV cache hit/miss (useful for batching audits)
- model_hash: short model commit hash or model-id
- rollout_id: optional pointer to rollout job if action relates to release
- evidence_refs: array of evidence filenames that accompany the event (e.g. RELEASE_EVIDENCE_...)

3) SIEM export and packaging notes
- Export cadence: immediate streaming (preferred) with 15s buffer on the Firehose lane; fallback to minute-aggregated files if downstream unavailable.
- Envelope format: newline-delimited JSON, gzip compressed in-flight, s3-tiered for replay. SIEM team asked for field names to be flat and stable for 12 months.
- Retention tags: add retention_policy: short|standard|long. Default for audit logs = standard (90d immediate, archive 7y).
- Correlation keys: ensure event_id and request_id are present for cross-system stitching.
- Test exports: run two sample exports (canary + full) and capture sample ids -> save under linked artifact: JIRA-SEC-4123.

4) Evidence automation (implementation plan)
- Trigger points: release creation, canary passed, canary failed, manual signoff, exception granted.
- Artefact list: rbacsnapshot.json, auditlogs-<range>.ndjson.gz, siem-export-metadata.json, signoff.csv, rollback-proof.txt
- Automation actions: upon release creation, CI job will collect snapshots and emit an evidence bundle to the evidence-store; release UI will show a download link and attach to the release ticket.
- Failure modes: if evidence bundle creation fails, block merge to prod branch and mark release as "evidence-failed" (manual override allowed by SecEng lead).

5) Exception approval flow (fast-path)
- Use case: emergency exception required to bypass a non-blocking RBAC deny for operational debug (non-customer-data access).
- Fast-path criteria: must be time-limited (max 4 hours), scoped, and logged; no escalation to legal/infosec if no PII touched.
- Approvals: two on-call approvals (SRE on-call + SecOps on-call) plus SecEng lead retro signoff within 24h.
- Audit requirements: create an exception record in the exceptions table (JIRA-SEC-XXXX), attach evidence bundle, and mark expiration timestamp.

6) Escalation matrix (who to call)
- On-call SRE: pager SRE primary (PagerDuty SRE-prod)
- SecOps on-call: pager SecOps primary
- SecEng lead: Sara Thompson (mobile:+1-415-555-0189)
- Release owner: Miguel Alvarez
- Product security: Priya Nair (for policy exceptions)

7) Dry run plan (this week)
- Monday: apply RBAC v2 policies to staging and run role tests (owner: eng-privsec).
- Tuesday: generate audit logs for 24h on staging and send SIEM dev export.
- Wednesday: run evidence automation pipeline for mock-release-2026-02 and validate bundle creation.
- Thursday: simulate fast-path exception and follow approval flow; ensure exception record is created and evidence attached.
- Friday: retro 30m with attendees: eng-privsec, release-eng, secops, product-security.

8) Signoff matrix (placeholders)
- Release Owner (eng): Miguel Alvarez — signoff: ________ date: ______
- Security Review (sec-eng): Sara Thompson — signoff: ________ date: ______
- SRE Readiness: On-call SRE — signoff: ________ date: ______
- Compliance Evidence: Audit owner (security) — signoff: ________ date: ______

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm exact retention_policy bucket names with infra (assigned: Omar).
- Do we need to include raw KV cache contents in evidence bundle? privacy concerns; recommend only keys and metadata. (discussion item)
- Verify whether model_hash should use full sha256 or shortened 8-char tag for privacy/perf.
- Coordinate end-to-end test with SIEM production ingest window to validate replayability.

Links / references:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/RBAC+v2+design+notes
- Jira: JIRA-SEC-4123 (SIEM export sample payloads)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1789 (audit log producer)

Notes to self: keep this doc terse — move canonical schemas into Confluence once the dry run is green. Capture screenshots of the canary rollback runbook in the evidence bundle.

---- end of notes ----
